lines.text: Neural networks are not new. The first one was built in 1958.
For more than fifty years they mostly did not work. Three things were missing.
One. Data. In 2009, researchers released ImageNet, more than a million labeled photos.
Two. Compute. In 2012, a network called AlexNet trained on just two graphics chips, and won the ImageNet contest by a wide margin.
Its error rate was 15 percent. The runner up was at 26.
Three. A design that scales. In 2017, a paper introduced the transformer.
It lets a model read a whole text at once, so adding more chips and more data keeps paying off.
Same old idea. Data, compute, and a design that scales. That is why it works now.
